name: com.unity.memoryprofiler
description: The Memory Profiler offers a unified solution allowing you to profile both small projects on mobile devices and big AAA projects on high end machines. It provides actionable information about allocations in the engine to allow developers to manage and reduce memory usage.

_upm.changelog:
### Added
- Added support for new kinds of managed roots in CoreCLR snapshots: thread's stack, pending finalizer, frozen or pinned memory. Those are now visible as roots and shown in the Roots & Impact view.
- Added filter-aware Impact values to the Roots & Impact table: when a search or status filter is active, rows that only remain visible because a descendant matches now show the impact of their filter-matching descendants as the primary value, with the row's own full impact shown struck-through and dimmed beside it, and the table total likewise reflects only the filter-matching entries.
- Added a note to the Memory Impact section of the Selection Details for *Unity Objects* stating whether the Native Object exclusively owns its Managed Shell (or vice versa) or if it only owns part of its impact due to shared references. The general explanation of Memory Impact now lives in a collapsible "What Is Memory Impact?" foldout that links to the documentation.
- Added a "Potential Savings" widget to the Summary page that surfaces the clearest avoidable memory — Leaked Managed Shells, Leaked dynamically created Assets, Unused Assets in loaded AssetBundles, Unloadable Assets, and Broken Script References — each measured by its memory Impact. For AssetBundles the figure is the memory that unloading — or repartitioning — the bundles would actually reclaim: their otherwise-unused contents plus the shaveable share of each bundle's own serialization size.
- Added deep-links from each Potential Savings widget row into the Roots & Impact view pre-filtered to that category's object statuses (via a per-row Inspect button, a double-click, or the widget's Inspect button and its Selection Details panel), so you can investigate and act on the found memory usage directly. The AssetBundles category opens the view expanded rather than flattened so you can assess bundle granularity.
- Added an option to the preferences to toggle the "Potential Savings" widget on the summary page between the default of focusing on the exclusive impact (which is guaranteed to be reducible by addressing the flagged issues) and the total impact (which encompasses memory usage which *might* be able to be reduced this way but can't be guaranteed to be reducible algorithmically at scale).
- Added the sums of size columns into their column headers.
- Added a "Scale bars to parent" option to the footer of the All Of Memory, Unity Objects and Roots & Impact tables and their comparison tables. It scales the size bars relative to the parent item instead of the table total (in the comparison tables, relative to the larger of the summed increases and summed decreases among its siblings, as a parent's net difference can be smaller than a child's), and toggling it keeps the current state of the table.
- Added Depth, Refs (referrers), Share (of impact) and Impact (total impact) columns to the References panel's "Referenced By" and "References To" tables, so you can more easily reason about where the impact is coming from, even if the references aren't rooted (and therefore listed as its children in the Roots & Impact table) to the selected item. Depth is shown relative to the currently selected item's shortest path to root (↑ = closer to the root, ↓ = further away, 0 = same depth), in brackets when a reference's shortest path terminates at a different root. Share shows a dash, with an explanation, when the selected item's own impact had already been fully attributed before the referrer distributed its memory, since none of it reached the selection in that case. Column visibility is remembered per rider for the session and defaults to sensible sets per rider (e.g. Refs and Share are only shown by default on "References To"). "Referenced By" and "References To" can be sorted by any column except "Flags" (formerly "!"), defaulting to Depth (or Impact when Depth is hidden), and the sort column and direction are remembered per rider for the session.
- Added a "Select In..." button to Selected Item Details, and a "Select In" submenu to the context menus of table rows, References rows
